In [[mathematics]], '''Chrystal's equation''' is a first order nonlinear [[ordinary differential equation]], named after the mathematician [[George Chrystal]], who discussed the [[singular solution]] of this equation in 1896.<ref>Chrystal G., "On the p-discriminant of a Differential Equation of the First order and on Certain Points in the General Theory of Envelopes Connected Therewith.", Trans. Roy. Soc. Edin, Vol. 38, 1896, pp. 803–824.</ref> The equation reads as<ref>Davis, Harold Thayer. Introduction to nonlinear differential and integral equations. Courier Corporation, 1962.</ref><ref>Ince, E. L. (1939). Ordinary Differential Equations, London (1927). Google Scholar.</ref>

:<math>\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + Ax \frac{dy}{dx} + By + Cx^2 =0</math>

where <math>A,\ B, \ C</math> are constants, which upon solving for <math>dy/dx</math>, gives

:<math>\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{A}{2} x \pm \frac{1}{2} (A^2 x^2 - 4By - 4Cx^2)^{1/2}.</math>

This equation is a generalization of some particular cases of [[Clairaut's equation]] since it reduces to a form of Clairaut's equation under certain conditions as given below.

==Solution==

Introducing the transformation <math>4By=(A^2-4C-z^2)x^2</math> gives

:<math>xz\frac{dz}{dx} = A^2 + AB - 4C \pm Bz - z^2.</math>

Now, the equation is separable, thus

:<math>\frac{z \, dz}{A^2 + AB - 4C \pm Bz - z^2} = \frac{dx}{x}.</math>

The denominator on the left hand side can be factorized if we solve the roots of the equation <math>A^2 + AB - 4C \pm Bz - z^2=0</math> and the roots are <math>a,\ b = \pm  \left[ B +\sqrt{(2A+B)^2 - 16C} \right]/2</math>, therefore

:<math>\frac{z \, dz}{-(z-a)(z-b)} = \frac{dx}{x}.</math>

If <math>a\neq b</math>, the solution is

:<math>x \frac{(z-a)^{a/(a-b)}}{(z-b)^{b/(a-b)}} = k</math>

where <math>k</math> is an arbitrary constant. If <math>a=b</math>, (<math>(2A+B)^2 - 16C=0</math>) then the solution is

:<math>x(z-a) \exp \left[\frac a {a-z}\right]=k.</math>

When one of the roots is zero, the equation reduces to a special-case of [[Clairaut's equation]] and a parabolic solution is obtained in this case, <math>A^2+ AB -4C=0</math> and the solution is

:<math>x(z\pm B)=k, \quad \Rightarrow \quad 4By = - AB x^2 - (k\pm Bx)^2.</math>

The above family of parabolas are enveloped by the parabola <math>4By=-ABx^2</math>, therefore this enveloping parabola is a [[singular solution]].
